page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It features 4.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities but limited multi-core and memory scaling. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance ranks in the top 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores fall in the middle 50%. However, multi-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores landing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, but small-block cached read bandwidth and overall Passmark memory scores are weak to poor, reflecting the low memory density.

This hardware profile offers a cost-effective option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without high memory demands. Due to the 1 GB of RAM per vCPU constraint, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale multi-threaded compilation. It is best utilized for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, text processing, or small-scale LLM text generation where memory footprint is minimal.
